equity_bridge.item: Commodity inventory at fair value less costs to sell
equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR capital-management note; readily marketable grain, oilseed, oil and tallow funded by the secured inventory facilities ($592.9m) that sit in net debt. Net debt less this item = core cash $171.2m, the company's own measure. Its funding cost is charged in the flows.

Management estimate $30-35m remaining for Release 1 (N&E, due 1H CY2027); excluded from Underlying EBITDA so charged here. Taken pre-tax at the top of the range because Release 2 is deferred and unquantified.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: nominal through-cycle growth (ECA production 10-year rolling average +2.7% a year, offset by declining share of crop captured); equity_5yr_cagr of 1.5% is the nearest historical anchor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: CAGRs are not meaningful for this business. FY26 EPS and owner FCF are negative, so EPS and FCF CAGRs are undefined; the 3-year windows start at the FY23 peak and the 5-year windows at FY21, so revenue reads -4.7% and +5.4% for the same company. Equity has shrunk since FY23 because distributions (dividends plus buy-backs) exceeded earnings. Revenue tracks grain prices, not earnings power.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; interest income not stripped because the group is in net debt): FY21 118.6, FY22 358.6, FY23 505.1, FY24 72.7, FY25 174.0, FY26 -52.9. The series is dominated by commodity-inventory swings and is not a growth series. SBC is immaterial (0.1-4.4m a year), so reported and owner FCF are within $5m in every year.

scenario_narratives.base: FY26 was a margin trough, not a volume trough: a 35.2mmt ECA crop still produced only $223m of Underlying EBITDA because a global wheat surplus pushed prices to multi-year lows and growers held grain back. FY27 starts with a smaller forecast crop (26.6mmt) but better export and crush margins, so earnings recover part of the way (about $257m), then reach management's through-the-cycle level of about $320m plus half the remaining transformation benefit by FY29 and grow with nominal revenue thereafter. The declining share of crop captured is offset by Animal Nutrition and Bulk Materials growth, so the through-cycle figure holds but does not rise in real terms. Owner FCF settles around $95-100m after leases, inventory funding cost, tax and roughly $70m of capex.
scenario_narratives.bull: The through-cycle earnings base turns out to be the $405m that the FY20-26 pro-forma record actually averaged rather than the $320m management is prepared to underwrite. Global grain balances tighten, crush margins return to through-cycle levels, the transformation program delivers the full $20-30m, Animal Nutrition keeps growing volumes near its 14% five-year rate and bulk materials lift port utilisation outside the grain season. Renewable-fuel feedstock demand is an option on top and is not in the numbers. Owner FCF settles around $140-150m.
scenario_narratives.bear: The through-cycle framework itself is eroding. Growers keep bypassing the network, so receivals and outloads fall regardless of crop size as they have since FY22; Bunge-Viterra and on-farm storage take share; crush margins stay below through-cycle on strong global oilseed supply; and with the Crop Production Contract cap exhausted there is no payout in a drought year before FY29. Average Underlying EBITDA is about $250-260m, the transformation program slips again, and capex falls to the sustaining level as sites close. Owner FCF settles around $60-70m and the business earns well below its cost of capital on a $1.3bn equity base.

valuation_philosophy.summary: GrainCorp is valued on normalized through-cycle earnings, neither the FY21-23 boom nor the FY26 trough. The trading book is treated as self-funding: commodity inventory offsets the facilities that finance it, the company's core cash is what reaches the bridge, and the interest on those facilities is charged as an operating cost. Cyclical and structural risk is carried by three earnings levels ($250-260m, about $330m, about $420m of Underlying EBITDA) and their weights, at one discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: The through-the-cycle EBITDA level is the whole valuation: each $10m of sustained Underlying EBITDA is worth roughly $0.35-0.40 a share
Management has given no quantified FY27 guidance (due at the February 2027 AGM); year-one margins are an estimate
Year-end commodity inventory and its funding are a seasonal low; a fall in grain prices between balance date and sale would reduce the $597m bridge item
Inventory funding cost is modelled as a fixed 0.8% of revenue; it rises with both interest rates and grain prices
Capex is held near ex-lease depreciation; a multi-year port or rail renewal program above that level is not modelled
The terminal multiple cap binds in every scenario (Gordon exceeds 11-14x), so the cap choice matters more than terminal growth

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 4.69-8.61
data_sources.financials: GNC.AX_Metrics.csv (FY2016-FY2026); FY2026 Annual Report (segment note, capital management note, lease note, cash flow statement); FY2026 results presentation (capex and D&A split, through-the-cycle slide, cash flow bridge)

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average diluted shares FY2026 (218,585,501; FY26 AR EPS note). Issued shares at 30 Sep 2026 were 217,078,049; the ~1.5m difference is unvested rights. Held flat: SBC is expensed in the flows and the buy-back (about $37m of the $75m program unspent) is not credited.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR statement of changes in equity, share-based payments $0.1m (FY25 $2.7m, FY22 peak $4.3m). FY26 is depressed by reversals on missed hurdles; the forward path uses 0.04% of revenue (about $3m), the FY22-25 average. No equity-award tax line (ASX, rights settled from treasury shares).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T05:10:12Z regular ASX close (Friday; valuation run on the weekend)
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD build: 10-year ACGB about 4.4% + 5.5% ERP x beta about 0.85 gives a cost of equity near 9.1%. Core debt is nil (core cash $171m) and the commodity-inventory facilities are charged as an operating carry cost inside the flows rather than treated as capital, so WACC is effectively the cost of equity: 9.0%. The same rate is used in all three scenarios; cyclicality and structural-erosion risk are carried in the flows and the weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. FY26 lease principal $44.3m + lease interest $9.4m = $53.7m is deducted inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities ($283.8m) are excluded from net debt (the company's net debt of $425.9m is borrowings less cash only). D&A in the tax build is ex-AASB 16: $74m of the $117m total (FY26 results presentation, capex and D&A slide).
inputs.inventory_funding_treatment: lease_cost_pct_path also carries the cost of funding the trading book. Commodity inventory ($597.1m at fair value less costs to sell, FY26 AR capital-management note) is added back in the equity bridge, which nets the year-end bridge to the company's own 'core cash' of $171.2m. Year-end is the seasonal low for inventory (H1 borrowings run about $1.7bn), so the matching cost is charged in the flows: net interest ex-leases $55.8m + interest income $11.1m (the cash that earns it is in the bridge) - about $9m on the $150m term debt (which is in net debt) = about $58m. Lease $53.7m + carry $58m = $111.7m = 1.57% of FY26 revenue.
inputs.normalized_fcf_anchor: The projection does not grow from last_fcf. FY26 reported FCF (-$52.8m) includes a $175m commodity-inventory build funded by $130m of facility drawdown and is a trough number; FY23 ($509m) was a peak with inventory unwinding. The base case converges on management's through-the-cycle Underlying EBITDA of about $320m plus part of the transformation uplift (4.4% of revenue, about $333m by FY29), which builds to owner FCF of roughly $95-100m a year: EBITDA 333 - lease and inventory carry 119 - D&A 79 = EBIT 135; tax at 30% 41; + D&A 79 - capex 72 - working capital 5.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (routing row 2: cyclical non-US operating company). Fresh build, no prior valuation. Revenue is a commodity pass-through, so margins are low single digits and the EBITDA margin path is the valuation; FY26 Underlying EBITDA of $223m (3.1%) is below management's through-the-cycle $320m and far below the FY21-23 peak of $331m-$703m. The FY2020 statutory profit includes the roughly $308m United Malt demerger gain and is not used anywhere. FY26 statutory EBITDA of $169.8m in the metrics history is after $36.9m transformation cost and the $16.2m GrainsConnect Canada sale loss; the model is built on Underlying EBITDA and charges the remaining transformation spend in the equity bridge. Historical EBITDA cells mix statutory and underlying by year. Australian franking credits are not valued. The 14cps final dividend (about $30m) declared after balance date is not deducted. The Crop Production Contract cap was reached in FY25: only the $6m annual premium remains through FY29 and it sits inside Underlying EBITDA. Buy-back cash in FY26 was $0.4m (FY25 $37.9m). House and street bases nearly coincide because SBC is about 0.04% of revenue; band_position is not informative here.

bear.ebitda_margin_note: Through-cycle earnings are structurally lower at about $250-260m (3.6% of revenue), roughly the FY24-26 average of $266m, which was earned on average-to-large crops. Capex is cut to the guided sustaining level as the site network is rationalised.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Underlying EBITDA as % of revenue: FY27 about $257m (smaller 26.6mmt ECA crop forecast but export and crush margins recovering from FY26 lows), FY28 about $301m, then 4.4% (about $333m in FY29) = management's $320m through-the-cycle figure plus roughly half of the remaining $10-20m transformation benefit. Deliberately below the $405m arithmetic FY20-26 pro-forma average, which FY22-23 pulls up.
base.capex_note: FY26 capex $74m (sustaining $54m, growth, ventures, transformation). Guided sustaining $40-50m; mature level 0.95% of revenue (about $70m) keeps capex close to ex-lease D&A ($74m).
base.wc_note: Non-commodity working capital consumes about 3% of revenue growth; commodity inventory itself is funded by the dedicated facilities and handled in the bridge.

bull.ebitda_margin_note: Through-cycle earnings settle near the $405m FY20-26 pro-forma average (5.3% of revenue, about $420m in FY29 dollars): full $20-30m transformation benefit, Animal Nutrition and Bulk Materials keep compounding, crush margins normalise. Still far below the FY22-23 peak of $565m-$703m; no boom year is capitalised.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted to 25% from the 15% house default: the last three years averaged $266m on average-to-large crops, share of crop captured has fallen every year since FY22, and the CPC no longer pays out in a drought. Base 50%: it rests on management's own stated through-the-cycle figure, which sits below the seven-year average. Bull cut to 25% from 35%: it needs the cycle average to hold at the FY20-26 level, which FY22-23 flattered, and it needs the twice-delayed transformation program to deliver in full.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
